title: Knowing the low does not soil the divine intellect
source_text: XX. Nec ideo vilescit intellectus divinus, quod nec parvas & viles cognoscat: sicut & sol non inquinatur, propterea quod illius radii saepe limum & stercora feriant & collustrent.
pass_a_gloss: Nor does the divine intellect therefore grow base because it knows small and vile things: just as the sun is not defiled because its rays often strike and light up mud and dung.
pass_b_english: Knowing low objects does not degrade God.
Sun analogy: rays on mud stay clean.

lemmas.gloss: Nor does the divine intellect therefore grow base

choices.english: just as the sun is not defiled
choices.why: Blocks the dignity objection to knowing vile particulars.
rejected: contact with base objects soils God’s mind
